        Play, build and learn Ifa Games and Orisa Games

        This is the gaming environment of Play IFA Games, at playifagames.org/env. One living Yorùbá world, with its seven Ifa Stadiums, plaza, market, accounts, coins and Learning Hall, is shared by every game. Ayò Ọlọ́pọ́nfá and Erélayé are live now. More games from the Ifa Games and Orisa Games families will arrive in the same world, some of them proposed by players here.

        Developer kit

        For programmers working with Play IFA Games. The full guide is docs/BUILDING-GAMES.md in the code.

        1. 1 · Register itAdd an entry to GAMES in packages/shared/src/games.ts: family, kind, blurb, icon. It appears here, on the title screen and in GET /v1/games as "coming".
        2. 2 · Write the rules engineA pure TypeScript package (see packages/ayo-engine) with no browser or server code, so the client and the server run the same rules.
        3. 3 · Give it a screenA panel in apps/web/src/html/panels, a module that renders it, and an entry in the router. Load it lazily.
        4. 4 · Place it in the worldA table, dais or building in world/build.ts with an interaction that opens the screen, like the Erélayé dais.
        5. 5 · Server and online playRoutes and storage behind /v1, a migration, and moves checked on the server for anything rated or rewarded.
        6. 6 · Test, review, go liveEngine tests from the primary source, staff review of rules and cultural content, then set its status to "live".

                            Ayò Ọlọ́pọ́nfá

                            Olójú Mẹ́rìndínlógún · the sixteen-pit Ifá board

                            Sow 128 seeds through sixteen pots named for the principal Odù, #1 Ogbè to #16 Òfún. Capture, chain captures and outwit the Oracle or a friend. The first board game of IfaGame of Life, Erélayé; more games and game families are on the way.

                            How to play

                            Every game is played at a real table in one of the seven Ifa Stadiums. Matchmaking pairs you with another player and seats you both at an open table; ranked games move your rating. Every stadium also has an Oracle table.

                            Ayò family Reference rules v1 · 2 players · 10–25 min · 16 Odù pots · 128 seeds

                            Ayò Ọlọ́pọ́nfá Olójú Mẹ́rìndínlógún

                            A sowing-and-capture game played on a sixteen-pit board shaped by the Ọpọ́n Ifá. Each pit carries the name of one of the sixteen principal Odù.

                            Each pot is an Odù

                            Ogbè opens your side of the board and Òfún closes the other: as seeds travel from pot to pot they pass through the sixteen principal Odù. In Play IFA each pot also carries a modern field of knowledge — a design theme of this game, not a teaching of Ifá.

                            Sow

                            Lift every seed from one of your pots and drop one in each following pot, counter-clockwise in number order: #1 → #8 along your row, then #9 → #16.

                            Capture

                            Finish in an opponent pit that reaches a capturing count and take those seeds.

                            Chain

                            Keep capturing backwards while the previous pits also qualify.

                            Play the Oracle

                            The Oracle sits at an Oracle table in every Ifa Stadium. AI never plays in ranked games.

                            Reference rules v1. The standard game from Òpè I to Ọ̀ta, as published for Ayò Ọlọ́pọ́nfá on playifagames.org. Every match in the world runs on this engine.

                            Seeds per pot
                            8 seeds per pot at the start (128 in all), shown as the 2-column × 4-row Odù Ifá pattern.
                            Sowing
                            Sow counter-clockwise, one seed per pot, in pot-number order (#1 → #16 → #1). On the board your row (#8 … #1) is on top and your opponent's (#16 … #9) below, so both rows run right to left. Skip your starting pot on full laps.
                            Capture
                            Your last seed lands in an opponent pot that now holds exactly 2 or 3 seeds.
                            Chain capture
                            The capture extends backward through consecutive opponent pots holding 2–3 seeds.
                            Grand Slam voided
                            If a capture would empty all of the opponent's pots, the entire capture is cancelled.
                            Starvation rule
                            You cannot leave your opponent with 0 seeds if it can be avoided. Suspended when 6 or fewer seeds remain.
                            Winning
                            Most seeds captured when a player has no legal moves. Remaining seeds go to each player's own side.
                            Veteran board
                            Àgbà-Ọ̀ta plays the veteran board: captures on exactly 4.

                                The IfaGame of Life

                                Erélayé is an Odù-based cellular automaton: Ifá’s parallel to Conway’s Game of Life. Each of the 256 cells on the 16 × 16 IfaField is one Odù Ifá. Its row gives the right leg and its column the left leg, so the sixteen Méjì run down the diagonal.

                                The law of each generation: a cell comes alive when exactly 3 of its 8 neighbours live, and stays alive with 2 or 3. Every other cell rests. The field wraps at its edges, so it has no border.

                                From these few laws come life, death, emergence, stillness (stasis) and rhythm (oscillation).

                                Its dual, Erékọ́layé, the Ifa Non-Game of Life, is in development at Play IFA Games and will join when its laws are published.

                                Source: Erélayé · Building Mode, playifagames.org. The field starts from the source’s generation 0.

                                                      Design language

                                                      The interface borrows from the Ọpọ́n Ifá: a fixed rim around a working field. Green and gold come from Ọ̀rúnmìlà's beads, the dark background from àdìrẹ indigo, and the light background from ìyẹ̀rọ̀sùn-dusted wood. Odù marks are the recurring motif.
